purpose: Every locked check on the platform in one line each, including those that failed. Written from the check reports and the scorecard summaries; nothing is computed here.

outcomes.disagrees: The comparison data disagree with the model
outcomes.failed: Candidate or tool rejected under its plan
outcomes.not_adopted: Partly consistent; not adopted under the plan's rule
outcomes.inconclusive: Cannot be decided from the data available

findings.question: Does Hughes 2019 predict how exposure rises with kidney impairment (CC-5013-PK-001)?
findings.headline: Mild consistent; moderate and severe exposure under-predicted.
findings.acceptance_rule: Simulated percentile: observed inside the 5th-95th percentile of simulated group values (between-subject variability only). Re-judged under acceptance rule v2 (12 November).

findings.question: Does Kim 2026 predict how exposure rises with kidney impairment (CC-5013-PK-001)?
findings.headline: Mild and moderate consistent; severe under-predicted in the primary scenario.
findings.acceptance_rule: Simulated percentile: observed inside the 5th-95th percentile of simulated group values (between-subject variability only). Re-judged under acceptance rule v2 (12 November).

findings.question: Do the first two results hold with virtual subjects matched to the study?
findings.headline: Hughes unchanged; Kim's consistent moderate result disappears. Both under-predict moderate and severe.
findings.acceptance_rule: Simulated percentile: observed inside the 5th-95th percentile of simulated group values (between-subject variability only). Re-judged under acceptance rule v2 (12 November).

findings.question: Do Hughes and Kim hold in myeloma patients (Bridoux 2016)?
findings.headline: Both under-predict moderate and severe again, so the non-cancer population of CC-5013-PK-001 does not explain the gap.
findings.acceptance_rule: Simulated percentile: observed inside the 5th-95th percentile of simulated group values (between-subject variability only). Re-judged under acceptance rule v2 (12 November).

findings.question: Does the elimination-pathway model, calibrated on normal kidney function, predict the impaired groups of the same study?
findings.headline: Secretion-preserved reading rejected. Intact-nephron reading consistent in mild, in severe in the primary scenario only, and under-predicts moderate (0.79 of observed AUC); the moderate result assumes all of the dose is absorbed.
findings.acceptance_rule: Confidence interval: model value inside the 95% CI of the observed mean (t, n-1).

findings.question: Does it extend to end-stage kidney disease on non-dialysis days?
findings.headline: Over-predicts 1.31-fold with no residual function, consistent at 5-10 mL/min; residual function of the subjects not reported.
findings.acceptance_rule: Confidence interval: model value inside the 95% CI of the observed mean (t, n-1). At residual CrCl 0, 5 and 10 mL/min.

findings.question: Does a model in which secretion falls faster than filtration fit better?
findings.headline: Three of four deciding comparisons consistent, so not adopted. The current model is consistent with both myeloma studies in moderate and severe impairment in the main scenario (Kim severe too high in 2 of 3 sensitivity scenarios) and predicts too much exposure in Bridoux's normal and mild groups.
findings.acceptance_rule: Confidence interval: model value inside the 90% CI of the observed geometric mean (Bridoux) or mean (Kim), t, n-1.

findings.question: Does the body map's one-compartment time course reproduce peaks and half-lives?
findings.headline: Peak under-predicted in every group, including normal (367 vs 568 ng/mL); half-life consistent in moderate and severe.
findings.acceptance_rule: Confidence interval: model value inside the 90% CI of the observed geometric mean (t, n-1).

findings.question: Does a two-compartment version, nothing fitted, do better?
findings.headline: Peak consistent in 2 of 4 groups (3 needed) and the moderate half-life got worse, so the body map keeps version 1.
findings.acceptance_rule: Confidence interval: model value inside the 90% CI of the observed geometric mean (t, n-1).

findings.question: Does the constant-clearance bortezomib model match Ogawa 2008 on days 1 and 11?
findings.headline: Day 1 exposure 2.9-fold too high; the rise from day 1 to day 11 is 1.9-fold against 5.1-fold observed.
findings.acceptance_rule: Confidence interval: model value inside the 95% CI of the observed mean (t, n-1).

findings.question: Does the Kuan 2012 model fix the day 1 to day 11 rise?
findings.headline: No: under neither reading of its saturable term does it reproduce the rise; candidate rejected.
findings.acceptance_rule: Confidence interval: model value inside the 95% CI of the observed mean (t, n-1).

findings.question: Does the model match a second study (CAN-1004, 72 h sampling)?
findings.headline: Day 1 consistent; day 11 under-predicted (127 vs 241 ng.h/mL). Both studies show a larger rise than a constant clearance allows.
findings.acceptance_rule: Confidence interval: model value inside the 95% CI of the observed mean (t, n-1).

findings.question: Can an empirical clearance that falls over repeated doses explain the rise?
findings.headline: Neither one-parameter form reached the CAN-1004 day 11 exposure, so neither was tested on Ogawa; candidates rejected.
findings.acceptance_rule: Confidence interval: model value inside the 95% CI of the observed mean (t, n-1).

findings.question: Does the Iwasaki 2020 target-binding PBPK model explain the rise?
findings.headline: No: day 1 over-predicted (107 vs 46.5 ng.h/mL), day 11/day 1 ratio 2.0 vs 5.1; it behaves like constant clearance. Candidate rejected.
findings.acceptance_rule: Confidence interval: model value inside the 95% CI of the observed mean (t, n-1).

findings.question: Does the model match a third study (MMY-3021, day 11)?
findings.headline: Day 11 exposure consistent only at the edge and not robust; peak under-predicted (111 vs 223 ng/mL).
findings.acceptance_rule: Confidence interval: model value inside the 95% CI of the observed mean (t, n-1).

findings.question: Does the model reproduce Reece 2011, the study its source compared it with?
findings.headline: Not reproduced: day 1 exposure about 2-fold too high at both doses; rise to day 11 1.5-fold against 2.4-3.1.
findings.acceptance_rule: Confidence interval: model value inside the 95% CI of the observed mean (t, n-1).

findings.question: Does the platelet model reproduce its own fitting data?
findings.headline: Consistent with the cycle 1 day 11 fall only with concentrations in ng/mL and the effect term as printed.
findings.acceptance_rule: Interval: primary ratio inside the plan's stated interval (0.58-0.72), numerically resolved.

findings.question: Does Gupta 2017 match the dedicated renal and hepatic impairment studies?
findings.headline: Myeloma with normal kidney function consistent; solid-tumour and hepatic groups under-predicted about 1.4-fold; peaks 2-4-fold low, so only AUC is shown.
findings.acceptance_rule: Simulated percentile: observed inside the 5th-95th percentile of simulated group values (between-subject variability only). Re-judged under acceptance rule v2 (18 November).

findings.question: Does Luo 2021 match GEN501 and SIRIUS first-dose data?
findings.headline: Peaks and 8 mg/kg AUC consistent; first-week AUC at 16 mg/kg over-predicted (observed 0.87 of model).
findings.acceptance_rule: Simulated percentile: observed inside the 5th-95th percentile of simulated group values (between-subject variability only).

findings.question: Does the result hold with each study's own demographics?
findings.headline: The 16 mg/kg over-prediction widens (0.83); the albumin effect predicts the two studies in the opposite order.
findings.acceptance_rule: Simulated percentile: observed inside the 5th-95th percentile of simulated group values (between-subject variability only). Re-judged under acceptance rule v2 (18 November).

findings.question: Can a curve built from the POMALYST label reproduce the label's own exposure?
findings.headline: The myeloma-only parameter set passes (Cmax 71.6 vs 75 ng/mL); the label's pooled clearance and volume ranges would predict about half and fail.
findings.acceptance_rule: Tolerance: model / label value within 0.67 to 1.5.

findings.question: Is the label curve consistent with the Li 2017 population model?
findings.headline: Consistent (AUC 860 vs Li 780; dialysis fold 1.38 in both). Model to model, not observed data.
findings.acceptance_rule: Tolerance, model to model: each ratio within 0.8 to 1.25.

findings.question: Can a one-compartment curve from the EVOMELA label reproduce its exposure?
findings.headline: Not eligible: peak under-predicted (3.64 vs 5.8 ug/mL), and the label's clearance and volume imply a 197-minute half-life against the stated 75.
findings.acceptance_rule: Tolerance: model / label value within 0.67 to 1.5.

findings.question: Can a curve from the HEMADY label reproduce its exposure?
findings.headline: Passes: clearance and AUC within 1%; peak 186 vs 247 ng/mL (ratio 0.75), within the plan's limits.
findings.acceptance_rule: Tolerance: model / label value within 0.67 to 1.5.

findings.question: Is the dexamethasone curve consistent with the NEOFORDEX studies?
findings.headline: Consistent on the primary endpoint and both AUCs; patients' apparent clearance was lower than the label's, a caveat shown with the curve.
findings.acceptance_rule: Confidence interval: model value inside the 95% CI of the observed mean (t, n-1). Geometric mean and CV converted on the log scale where reported that way.

findings.question: Does the rule-based eligibility extractor meet its accuracy thresholds?
findings.headline: All eight criterion types failed (precision 0.73-0.83, recall 0.64-0.80); version 2 was planned with a new 200-trial sample.
findings.acceptance_rule: Pass rule: precision >= 0.95 (Wilson lower bound >= 0.90) and recall >= 0.85 (lower bound >= 0.75), at least 20 pairs per type.

findings.question: Does the kidney-pathway result hold across the bioavailability the data allow (90-100% absorbed)?
findings.headline: No single bioavailability fits every study. At 90% the source study's moderate group becomes consistent, but its severe group, Bridoux's moderate group and the end-stage prediction fit worse; at 100% the reverse. Both bands are now marked as depending on absorption, and "faster than proportional" is not established.
findings.acceptance_rule: Confidence interval: model value inside the 95% CI of the observed mean (t, n-1). For CC-5013-PK-001; 90% CIs for Bridoux and Kim as in 2.0d; at each bioavailability.

findings.question: Do the four published-model kidney-function verdicts hold when the uncertainty of the published estimates is added?
findings.headline: Hughes: every verdict holds, moderate and severe under-predicted by a wide margin. Kim: most moderate and severe verdicts become indeterminate (observed within 1-4% of the widened limit); only Bridoux severe stays under-predicted.
findings.acceptance_rule: Acceptance rule v2: simulated percentile with published parameter uncertainty (bootstrap-matched, 200 sets x 50 trials), five seeds; indeterminate within 5% of a limit or when seeds disagree.

findings.question: Does the rule-based eligibility extractor v1.1 meet the plan v2 accuracy rule on 200 new trials, annotated blind?
findings.headline: No type passes. ECOG comes closest (precision 0.88, recall 0.89); kidney function, creatinine, bilirubin and AST/ALT have precision 0.71-0.81 and recall 0.68-0.76. Agreement is with one annotator's reading.
findings.acceptance_rule: Pass rule: precision >= 0.90 (Wilson lower bound >= 0.80) and recall >= 0.80 (lower bound >= 0.70), at least 30 pairs per type; pair-based measures.

findings.question: Does a language-model extractor (Claude Fable, frozen prompt) meet the plan v2 accuracy rule on the same 200 blind trials, and how does it compare with rule-based v1.1?
findings.headline: No type passes. Pair-based recall is higher than v1.1 for kidney function (0.82 against 0.72), platelets and ECOG; pair-based precision is similar. The two runs give the same status, comparator, value and unit on 1,596 of 1,600 answers (658 of 661 where a threshold was annotated): limited repeatability, not accuracy. Both extractors disagree with the reference on the same 13-33 pairs per type; this does not say whether the reference, the text or both extractors are wrong. A blind re-reading of the reference and an independent second annotator are planned before either extractor is revised.
findings.acceptance_rule: Plan v2 pass rule applied to run 1 (precision >= 0.90, lower bound >= 0.80; recall >= 0.80, lower bound >= 0.70; pair-based measures); run 2 for repeatability; paired with v1.1 without a superiority test.

findings.question: How much of the two extractors failing every type is the reference annotation rather than the extractors?
findings.headline: The single-annotator reference does not hold at the plan v2 bar. In a blind re-reading of the shared-error pairs and 50 seeded controls (215 of 216 items completed), the locked reading matched the original annotation in 27 of 160 shared pairs and 44 of 50 controls; 103 of 165 decided shared pairs were corrected and 28 called unclear, against 5 of 50 corrected and none unclear in the controls. Re-scoring the frozen outputs against the corrected reference moves v1.1 from 0 of 8 types passing to 3 of 8 where unclear pairs keep the original annotation and 7 of 8 where they are excluded, and the language model from 0 of 8 to 2 of 8 and 4 of 8; with the five post-lock pairs set aside, 6 of 8 and 4 of 8. The original blind results stay primary: both extractors failed. The decision step was not blind, because the original annotation and both answers were visible before each decision, so the corrected figures are not extractor accuracy; and the 5 corrections among 50 controls show a reference error rate outside the ambiguous pairs. Whether a single-annotator reference can judge an extractor at all is decided by the independent second annotator (intelligence_store/data/eligibility_second_annotation_plan_v1.json), not by this analysis.
findings.acceptance_rule: None applied. The plan fixes a post hoc corrected-reference sensitivity analysis with the same frozen outputs, the same scorer and the same plan v2 pass rule reported side by side for both extractors; the original blind results stay primary and unchanged.

findings.question: Is a reference annotation made by one reader reliable enough to judge an extractor at the plan v2 precision bar?
findings.headline: Two independent readers of the same 50 trials agree on 357 of 400 trial-and-type pairs (89.25%), with a trial-level bootstrap 95% interval of 84.75% to 93.5%. The plan's rule reads the lower bound against a 0.90 bar, so the reading is NOT ADEQUATE: a single-annotator reference is not shown to be reliable enough to judge an extractor at the plan v2 precision bar, and the plan's next step is an adjudicated two-annotator reference before either extractor is revised. The point estimate sits on the bar and the interval is wide because 50 trials cannot resolve it, which the plan anticipated; this is a failure to demonstrate adequacy, not a demonstration of wide disagreement. Detection agreement is high (kappa 0.93): the readers almost always agree on whether a threshold is stated, and differ on its detail. Per type, exact agreement runs from 0.84 (kidney function, AST/ALT) to 0.96 (ECOG). Descriptively, and on 50 trials only, both extractors pass none of the eight types against either reader's reference, so neither extractor's failure is an artefact of the owner's annotation. The 43 disagreements go to adjudication under the plan.
findings.acceptance_rule: Prespecified in the plan: the lower bound of the trial-level bootstrap 95% interval of overall exact agreement against a 0.90 bar. Below it, the reference is not adequate at that bar and an adjudicated two-annotator reference comes before either extractor is revised. Observed lower bound 0.8475.

findings.question: When the two readers disagreed, which reading was right?
findings.headline: Of the 43 pairs the two readers disagreed on, annotator B’s reading stands in 24, the owner’s in 9, and 10 are unclear. B’s reading won in every cause class, including 5 of 7 on comparator equality and 7 of 11 where one reader found a value the other missed, and 7 of 7 on kidney function. So the reference annotation is wrong in at least 24 of the 400 pairs and B’s reading in at least 9 — the reader who wrote the guide was wrong about 2.7 times as often as the reader applying it for the first time. These are lower bounds, and the floor is higher than the split shows: 7 of the 10 unclear decisions say in their reason that both readings were wrong, which the three choices could not express, so the reference is wrong in at least 31 pairs and B’s reading in at least 16. Errors the two readers share are invisible to adjudication altogether, and the re-reading of 14 November showed such errors exist. This does not rehabilitate or condemn either extractor: it measures the readers. It confirms from a second, independent direction the two defects the re-reading found, missed values and dropped equality, and it leaves the second-annotation verdict unchanged — a one-reader reference is not shown adequate at the plan v2 bar. An adjudicated reference is not produced here; that is a new annotation version under its own plan.
findings.acceptance_rule: None. The plan fixes the procedure, not a threshold: each disagreeing pair ends as the owner’s reading, annotator B’s, or unclear, with a reason. The counts are descriptive and are lower bounds on each reader’s errors, because only disagreements are adjudicated.

findings.question: Do the Gupta 2017 ixazomib and second Luo 2021 daratumumab verdicts hold when the uncertainty of the published estimates is added?
findings.headline: Ixazomib: 19 of 20 verdicts hold under every uncertainty scenario; severe renal impairment AUC becomes indeterminate (observed 0.4% above the widened limit), and hepatic-study exposure stays under-predicted. Daratumumab: the three Cmax verdicts hold; GEN501 16 mg/kg AUC0-7d, over-predicted before, and SIRIUS AUCinf become undecided: the first sits about 5% below the widened limit, the margin itself, the second is consistent in 24 of 25 runs.
findings.acceptance_rule: Acceptance rule v2, plan v2.1: simulated percentile with published parameter uncertainty converted from %RSE (decision 0004), five seeds, indeterminate within 5% of a limit or when seeds disagree; five uncertainty scenarios (independent, two correlation, normal on the natural scale, RSE at the top of its rounding), and a verdict that changes between them is read as undecided.

findings.question: Under annotation guide v3, do two readers agree well enough for a reference to judge an extractor at the plan v2 precision bar?
findings.headline: The owner and annotator B, reading the same fresh 50 trials alone under annotation guide v3, agree on 378 of 400 trial-and-type pairs (94.5%), with a trial-level bootstrap 95% interval of 91.25% to 97.0%. The plan's rule reads the lower bound against a 0.90 bar, so the reading is ADEQUATE: a two-reader reference under guide v3 is shown reliable enough to judge an extractor at that bar, and an adjudicated annotation version may now be built under its own plan. The margin is small: the lower bound clears the bar by 1.25 points on 50 trials. Detection agreement is high (kappa 0.96). Per type, exact agreement runs from 0.88 (ECOG) to 0.98 (kidney function, creatinine). Scored as written (comparison v1) the result is the same. Round one's trials were different, so only the bar compares, not the numbers. The owner annotated all 200 trials in the original pass and is not a naive reader; B is. Errors both readers share cannot be found this way. Descriptively, on 50 trials, the extractors have too little data on seven types; on ECOG, extractor v1.1 passes against the owner's reading and fails against B's, and the LLM extractor fails against both. No extractor is adopted or revised on this.
findings.acceptance_rule: Prespecified in plan v2.1: the lower bound of the trial-level bootstrap 95% interval of overall exact agreement (comparison v2, 2000 resamples, seed 20261122, trials in sorted order) against a 0.90 bar. At or above it, a two-reader reference under guide v3 is adequate at that bar. Observed lower bound 0.9125.

findings.question: Can a one-compartment curve from the KYPROLIS label reproduce its own Table 21 exposure for both 30-minute regimens?
findings.headline: Not eligible: the label's exposure and its stated clearance disagree about two-fold. Clearance from the 20/70 steady-state AUC is 90 L/h at 1.8 m2 (80 to 100 L/h across 1.6 to 2.0 m2), outside the stated 151-263 L/h, and that curve over-predicts the 20/56 peak 1.54-fold. A curve at the stated clearance (199 L/h) under-predicts every Table 21 AUC about 0.45-fold. The two regimens imply the same clearance (90 and 95 L/h), so the reading of average daily AUC holds; the disagreement is in the label. Carfilzomib stays at Knowledge only, and no label curve is shown.
findings.acceptance_rule: Prespecified: the first parameter set passing all eight checks at 1.8 m2 is used; ratio checks pass within 0.67 to 1.5, and clearance must fall inside the stated 151-263 L/h.

findings.question: Blind: do the constant-clearance and Iwasaki 2020 models match a fourth study (NCT01801436, Taiwan, n = 10) whose values were unread when the plan was locked?
findings.headline: No for both. Day 11 AUC (observed 190 ng.h/mL, 95% CI 151-230): constant clearance 127, under-predicted under every reading, reproducing the CAN-1004 under-prediction in the first blind study; Iwasaki 145, under-predicted under the primary reading but consistent at the smaller assumed body (158 at 50 kg), so not robust. Both under-predict the day 11 peak (84 and 60 vs 127) and over-predict day 11 clearance and Vss; both match the day 1 peak (83 and 52 vs 76). Not blind: day 11/day 1 AUC ratio 3.7 observed vs 1.6 and 1.5.
findings.acceptance_rule: Confidence interval: model value inside the 95% CI of the observed mean (t, n-1).

supersedes.change: Adds the blind NCT01801436 bortezomib result for the constant-clearance and Iwasaki models.
